- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true outcome over 10+ days, apply a 1–3% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.4+), reduce forecast smoothness and apply a 0.5–1% lag correction to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to next forecast.
